name: Kavet

anatomy.part: hook at the top of the shaft, where the yarn is caught
hub of the whorl, the shaft passing through its centre
upper right rim of the whorl face
foot of the shaft, the spindle's point
lower left rim of the whorl, where the yarn winds off
the yarn running up and left from the whorl, its first bend
far trailing end of the yarn, up and to the left
knot in the yarn hanging below the whorl
loose end of yarn hanging below the knot

myth: Mother Hesk sat at the pole with her spindle, drawing the string out thin and winding it on the whorl so the islands would not drift. Then Aun came with his knife, wanting to know how far the wind went. He cut, and the string went slack in her hand, but the spindle kept turning anyway, because a whorl does not know it has been cut. The yarn it still held ran off up and to the left, long as a fishing line, and no one has found its end. The Gulls say the loose end is still in Hesk's fist and she is counting the turns. When your own thread snags on the rocks, do not curse it. Hesk spins it still, and her count is patient. Sil looks down at the whorl sometimes from the Drowned Lantern and says nothing, which from Sil is a kindness. Keep your hands busy. A spindle that stops is a spindle that falls.
verse:
Hesk turns the whorl still
the loose yarn runs up and left
count what the knife missed
